desc: Ideation: reduce query (R,X) to max{dp[i] : i ≤ R, A_i ≤ X} where dp[i] is standard LIS-ending-at-i; single max-BIT sweep suffices
Parse input, coordinate-compress all A_i values (sorted unique), and store queries with their original indices.
Implement a Fenwick tree supporting prefix-max query and point update (take max at index, propagate upward).
Sweep index i=1..N: dp = 1 + bit.query(pos(A_i)-1); bit.update(pos(A_i), dp); answer all queries with R_i = i via bit.query(bisect_right(vals, X)).
Store answers by query index and print them in order.
Verify edge cases: duplicate values (strict increase via pos-1), X mapping via bisect_right, single-element prefixes; complexity O((N+Q) log N).
